note: Zero Financial (Zerocard), San Francisco; the firm lists a 2016 Seed entry, and the company closed a $20M Series A in May 2019, which graduates the row. Avant bought Zero Financial in April 2021. The Wikidata JP country was a one-word name match (disputed); the 20VC book's Zero is a different company (Helsinki CRM).
ZeroFox, Baltimore; listed through a SPAC in 2022 and taken private by Haveli Investments in 2024 for about $350M (Wikipedia), so acquired below $1B.

Zhone's Form 10 (2003) says it began operations in September 1999 on a $500M commitment from its initial investors including NEA, issued as Series A preferred in November 1999; the round is consortium-sized (KKR, TPG) but the record names it Series A. Zhone became DASAN Zhone Solutions (2016) then DZS, which filed Chapter 7 in March 2025; its assets went to an MSNi-owned Zhone Technologies in June 2025 (Data Center Dynamics), so acquired out of insolvency. Same company as the row dasan-zhone-solutions-inc.

Ziarco, a Sandwich (Kent) biotech of ex-Pfizer scientists, bought by Novartis in December 2016. Its first $6M came from BVF and Pfizer Venture Investments in 2012 without NEA; the round NEA joined in 2014 is not named in any source found, so the stage is undetermined.

The first round naming NEA is the July 2013 $4.1M Series A led by Columbus Nova; the November 2012 seed is credited to angels. The firm's 2012 year is read as the close year, hence medium confidence. Acquired by Logi Analytics in June 2019; the Accel book agrees on status.
Zosano Pharma, Fremont; filed Chapter 11 in 2022 and sold its assets, so acquired below $1B.

The firm lists a 2012 Seed entry; Foley Hoag's client note (2014-03-04) names Zumper's Series A financing, which graduates the row. Private, below $1B (last reported round $60M Series D in 2020); agrees with the a16z and Headline books.

Zuoyebang, Beijing (CN confirmed by the firm's own page). NEA's first year is 2018, when the company was already past its 2015 Series A and later rounds (Coatue led the July 2018 $350M Series D), so the entry is Growth. Mark aligned with the Coatue and Tiger Global books: $9.6B post-money on the December 2020 E+ round (EqualOcean), stale and before China's 2021 tutoring rules.
Zyngenia, Gaithersburg (Zybody bispecific antibodies); Form D rounds to 2012 and the firm's listing only to 2015. No later report of a sale, shutdown or financing was found, so the state is unknown.
3Jam, group SMS messaging, on the firm's 2008 US list only. Google News carries nothing on it; no city, fate or round could be established.

Acorn Cardiovascular (CorCap cardiac support device), St. Paul, Minnesota; it ceased operations after the device failed to win FDA approval (from knowledge, not re-verified). No round naming NEA was found.
Acoustic Imaging Technologies, Tempe, Arizona, ultrasound systems; the firm's historical list gives the exit as acquired by Dornier. No round naming NEA was found.
Actelis Networks, carrier broadband over copper, principal office Fremont, California (R&D in Israel); listed on Nasdaq (ASNS) since 2022. The round NEA entered is not on record.
Actional, web services management software, Mountain View; acquired by Progress Software in 2006 (the firm's historical list agrees). No round naming NEA was found.
Adaptec, Milpitas, storage controllers; listed 1986, its business sold to PMC-Sierra in 2010 (the Lightspeed book agrees). The 1980s round NEA entered is not on record.

NEA joined the $50M Series A led by Index and Interlagos (TechCrunch, April 2025); the founder's own $10M preceded it and there was no outside seed. In May 2026 the company rebranded as Cowboy Space Corporation (in-orbit compute and launch) and raised a $275M Series B at a $2B valuation (Payload), fresher than the a16z book's below-$1B reading. Same company as the row cowboy-space.
Agami Systems (formerly Zambeel), Sunnyvale, NAS storage; it shut down (Mercury News, 2008-08-20, 'What went wrong at start-up Agami Systems?'). No round naming NEA was found.

Agility Design Solutions, formed in 2008 from Catalytic Inc. and Celoxica's ESL tools business, DSP design software; its product lines went to Mentor Graphics in 2009 (from knowledge). No round naming NEA was found.
Agitar Software, Mountain View, Java developer testing; wound down around 2008. Aligned with the Sequoia book.
Akashic Memories, San Jose, sputtered thin-film disk media; the firm's historical list gives the exit as acquired by Kubota. No round naming NEA was found.

Alkermes, Inc. (Waltham, Massachusetts) combined with Elan Drug Technologies in 2011 and became a subsidiary of Alkermes plc (Dublin, Nasdaq ALKS); kept acquired under the successor-entity rule. The 1980s round NEA entered is not on record.

AllyAlign Health, Richmond, Virginia, Medicare Advantage plans for senior living. NEA led a new investment with Oak HC/FT, Town Hall Ventures and existing investors Heritage Group and Ziegler (company release, 2021-06-10; $300M per Fierce Healthcare), a syndicated financing rather than a control purchase; the firm's own archived page labels it Growth. The firm's May 2022 post says AllyAlign was combined with Elite Patient Care and Provider Health Services into Curana Health (row curana-health), so acquired by merger.

Alsius, Irvine, intravascular temperature management; went public through a SPAC merger in 2007 and sold its assets to ZOLL Medical in 2009. Its 2006 S-1 shows NEA VII holding Series C-D, E and F preferred, but a recapitalisation left the earlier series near zero, so NEA's first round is not established.

funding_rounds.round: Series C-D (exchanged from C-1, C-2 and D)

note: Alta Devices, Sunnyvale, thin-film GaAs solar; acquired by Hanergy in 2014. No round naming NEA was found.
Amplica, microwave amplifiers, on the firm's historical list as NASDAQ: AMPI; its later fate could not be established from the sources available (pre-web era).
Anadys Pharmaceuticals, San Diego; listed 2004, acquired by Roche in 2011 for about $230M. The round NEA entered is not on record.
Aprius, Sunnyvale, PCIe I/O virtualization; wound down around 2012. Aligned with the Lightspeed and Menlo books.

Mountain View design-analytics startup of Ranjitha Kumar; the $1.875M seed was led by NEA and a16z (University of Illinois news, 2016-07-21), while the firm's archived page gives 2014 as the year. Defunct, aligned with the a16z book. Graduation left for the graduation pass.
Arch Rock, San Francisco, IP-based wireless sensor networks; acquired by Cisco in 2010 (from knowledge). No round naming NEA was found.

AutoImmune Inc. (oral tolerance therapies, Nasdaq AIMM), founded in Lexington, Massachusetts and later run from Pasadena after its trials failed in the late 1990s; its final fate could not be established.

AVOS Systems, the Chad Hurley and Steve Chen company (Delicious, MixBit); FinSMEs reported its Series A in April 2012, the year the firm gives, but the page could not be read to confirm NEA in it, hence low confidence. Delicious was sold in 2014; the company's later state is unknown.
AXYS Pharmaceuticals (Arris and Sequana merged in 1998), South San Francisco; acquired by Celera Genomics in 2001. The round NEA entered is not on record.

Bandgap Engineering, Woburn, Massachusetts, nanostructured silicon for PV and Li-ion anodes; the firm's page ran to 2021 as private. No report of its later state or of the round NEA entered was found (Google News returns only the physics term).

Banjo, real-time event detection from social and public data, Park City, Utah; renamed SafeXai in 2020 after its founder's resignation and still reported operating in 2021 (Salt Lake Tribune). The round NEA entered in 2015 is not named in any source found.
Bariatric Partners (Journey Lite surgery centers), on the firm's 2008 list only; Google News has nothing on it, and no city, fate or round could be established.

Be Inc. (BeBox and BeOS), Menlo Park; listed 1999, its assets bought by Palm in 2001 and the company dissolved. The Wikidata IL country was a one-word name match (disputed). The round NEA entered in 1996 is not on record.

Belmont Technology was the placeholder name of Onshape (Wikipedia): the same company as the row onshape. Cloud CAD, Cambridge, Massachusetts; acquired by PTC in November 2019 for $470M. Its first $9M came from North Bridge and Commonwealth without NEA; the round NEA joined in 2013 is not named.

funding_rounds.lead: North Bridge Venture Partners, Commonwealth Capital

note: BENU, integrated health benefits for mid-size employers, first invested 2000. Not the Spark book's Benu (Benu Networks, broadband software, Billerica): a name collision. No city, fate or round could be established.

Bethesda Research Laboratories, Gaithersburg, Maryland; combined with GIBCO in 1983 to form Life Technologies (row life-technologies), as the firm's historical list says. No round naming NEA was found.

BlackBird, a California flight-sharing marketplace founded by Rudd Davis in 2016; NEA led its $10M Series A (announced March 2019; the firm's 2018 year is the close year). Not the a16z and USV books' Blackbird (Blackbird Labs, New York restaurant loyalty): a name collision. Its current state and exact city could not be established.

Blispay, Baltimore consumer point-of-sale credit; the firm's archived page labels the 2014 investment seed. Acquired by Alliance Data in May 2019 (Baltimore Business Journal). Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Bridge International Academies, low-cost school chain founded in Nairobi in 2008; Wikipedia lists NEA among its investors and names NewGlobe Schools, Inc. as its parent. NewGlobe is the company's own restructured parent, not an acquirer, so the prefilled acquired is disputed: private. Same company as the row newglobe. The round NEA entered in 2012 is not named.
British Biotechnology (British Biotech plc from its 1992 listing), Oxford; merged with RiboTargets into Vernalis in 2003 (Wikipedia). The round NEA entered is not on record.
CaMaRa launched from Copenhagen on 2026-09-09 with a seed financing from Forbion, Novo Holdings, NEA and RA Capital (company release); inside the censoring window.

Cape Productions, an end-to-end drone video service the firm first backed in 2014. Not the a16z, Bain Capital Ventures and IVP books' Cape (privacy mobile carrier, Washington): a name collision. Its fate, city and the round NEA entered could not be established.
